text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Bulgaria's exiled King Simeon II is expected to arrive in the country on Tuesday to mark the 118th anniversary of the the first Bulgarian constitution, the king'g press office said.
-- Bulgaria is expected to sell six state owned banks by the year-end, deputy prime minister Alexander Bozhkov said. @
-- Bulgaria expects to receive $22.5 million from Russia under an accord for the reconstruction of Russian-made reactors at the Kozloduy nuclear power plant, an energy expert said.

-- Bulgaria is expected to introduce compulsory AIDS tests for all foreigners staying more than one month in the country in a bid to prevent the spread of the disease, a Health ministry senior official said. @

-- Bulgaria's prime minister Stefan Sofianski is expected to leave for Moscow today to discuss a new agreement for transit of Russian natural gas via Bulgaria and trade liberalisation issues with his Russian counterpart Viktor Chernomyrdin.
-- Bulgaria has received $19 million from international lenders to finalise the restoration of private land ownership, Agriculture minister Roumen Hristov said. @
-- Bulgaria's interim government is expected to discuss today the possible sale of a 75 percent stake in Bulgaria's biggest oil refinery Neftochim, the newspaper said without quoting sources.
-- Bulgaria's Foreign minister Stoyan Stalev is expected to leave for Greece today for talks on boosting Greek investments in Bulgaria with his Greek counterpart Theodoros Pangalos.

-- The US General Electric was interested in buying Bulgaria's state owned Varna coal-fired power plant and export electricity to Turkey, a Bulgarian energy expert said. @ -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
